sources.entry: Lessons Learned in Software Development: one of those articles that give you years of hard-earned lessons, all in one short article. Must read.

summary.title: Lessons Learned in Software Development
summary.one_liner: A list of 22 practical heuristics for development, troubleshooting, cooperation and career, such as starting small, changing one thing at a time, and reproducing bugs before fixing them.
keywords: change one thing at a time
everything takes longer than you think
fix known errors then see what's left
takeaways: Build a very simple version first and extend it step by step, rather than planning everything up front.
Make small, single-change iterations and commit refactorings separately from new features to make problems easier to locate.
Add logging and error handling from the start, and make sure every new line of code is executed at least once during testing.
When troubleshooting, reproduce the problem first, fix known bugs before chasing remaining symptoms, and treat apparent coincidences as real causes.
Collaborate face to face where possible, explain problems aloud to colleagues, and keep learning through new tools, books and courses.
summary.summary: The article is a personal list of 22 heuristics for software development, grouped under development, troubleshooting, cooperation and miscellaneous. Each item gives a short rule of thumb with a brief justification and sometimes an example, such as temporarily misspelling a column name to trigger a database error handler. It also cites a few quotes, including John Gall on evolving from simple working systems and Hofstadter's Law on estimates. The tone is informal and experience-based rather than formal or research-driven.
